html:
Lombardy is the plain of northern Italy around Milan. On the map from 1783 to 1815 it is the old Duchy of Milan, ruled by Austria since 1714, then reshaped by the French.

It was one of the richest farming and silk regions in Europe, and Austrian rule in the 1700s brought land surveys, tax reform and new schools.

In 1796 Napoleon drove the Austrians out. Milan became the capital of the Cisalpine Republic and then of a Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy, with Napoleon as king. In 1815 the Congress of Vienna gave Lombardy back to the Austrian Empire, joined with Venetia as the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

Milan rose against Austria in 1848 but was retaken. In 1859 France and the Kingdom of Sardinia beat Austria at the Battle of Solferino, and Lombardy passed to Sardinia. Two years later it was part of the new Kingdom of Italy.
sum: Lombardy is the plain of northern Italy around Milan. On the map from 1783 to 1815 it is the old Duchy of Milan, ruled by Austria since 1714, then reshaped by the French.
